Cultural Phenomenon?
subhed: The evolution of the Frozen franchise in Japan

intro.text: Once upon a time, in a world swept away by magic and melody, Frozen captured hearts everywhere with its timeless tale of love, courage and self-acceptance. With unforgettable songs, beloved characters and a warmth that resonated across generations, Frozen didn’t just tick the boxes of a Disney classic; it became a worldwide sensation.

In Japan, Frozen became a cultural moment of its own. This remarkable success was no coincidence; it was a beautiful story brought to life with every facet of The Walt Disney Company — from studio production to merchandise and theme park experiences — working in harmony.

transition: So, let us pull back the curtain and discover the magic behind the momentum.
scrollyintro: The original Frozen film debuted in November 2013, and quickly became an Oscar®-winning, US$1.29 billion blockbuster. In Japan, the film shattered box office records within just two months of its theatrical release in March 2014, surpassing 20 billion yen to set a new milestone for Walt Disney Studios Japan.

text: Two charming animated shorts – Frozen Fever (2015) and Olaf’s Frozen Adventure (2018) – kept the excitement alive as fans eagerly awaited Frozen II’s arrival in 2019. For Disney’s 100th anniversary in 2023, the 2D dubbed version of Frozen was shown in 100 cinemas worldwide, inviting families to relive the magic alongside beloved Disney classics.
The adventures of Anna and Elsa have also been weaved into the very fabric of our parks, where over 26 million guests each year create unforgettable experiences at Tokyo Disneyland and DisneySea.

The first “Anna and Elsa’s Frozen Fantasy” seasonal event in 2015 drew massive crowds to the park. In 2024, the Frozen Kingdom even found a home in the new Fantasy Springs-themed port at Tokyo DisneySea, where guests can enjoy the sights, tastes and fun of Arendelle.

By the end of 2014, more than 2.2 million copies of the Frozen MovieNEX Blu-ray and DVD found their way into family homes around the world. Adults and kids alike can now sing along with their favorite characters, all from the comfort of their own homes.

The wonder of Frozen truly came alive through its music. The soundtrack rose to #1 in its 12th week of release, selling over 150,000 copies a week. Today, just the YouTube streams of “Let It Go” alone have crossed three billion. With Japan-exclusive CD and digital albums like Frozen THE BEST, its music continues to inspire new generations.

With marvelous Frozen games, fans can experience Arendelle’s magic first-hand. Young players joined Olaf on his whimsical quests in the 2015 Nintendo 3DS game Frozen: Olaf’s Gift, while gamers delighted in a thrilling crossover when the world of Frozen made its debut in SQUARE ENIX’s action RPG Kingdom Hearts III in 2019.

Disney’s most popular sisters even appeared as new Tsums in LINE: Disney Tsum Tsum in 2020. When the music game app New World Frozen launched in the following year, fans got to interact with their beloved film in whole new ways.
With 130 cable TV platforms and 5.3 million households tuning into the Disney Channel, the Frozen franchise continues to capture audiences in their living room.
In 2016, just two years after the first film, viewers continued the journey with the LEGO animated special, Frozen Northern Lights, which aired on Disney Channel and on terrestrial TV.

The Frozen fandom is a vibrant and dynamic community that spans the globe. It shines brightly in Japan, from children dressing up as Elsa and Anna at our parks, to adults sharing their creativity through fan art and cosplay at conventions.

From enchanting storybooks and engaging learning materials to colorful magazines, Frozen captivates young readers through the beautiful pages of Disney publications, with over 31 million copies published annually. Digital asset licensing further expands its reach, ensuring the wonder of Frozen is accessible in countless ways.
From dazzling Disney on Ice performances to beloved stage musicals, Frozen has become a spectacular live experience for millions.
The Shiki Theatre Company’s production, which opened in June 2021, celebrated its 1,000th performance in 2024. It is now a cherished and enduring part of Japan’s theater scene.
The mesmerizing world of Frozen is a cornerstone of Disney’s retail magic, connecting with millions of fans across Japan each year through physical and digital storefronts.
Customers have fallen under the spell of breathtaking dresses inspired by Elsa and Anna, making dreams come true through our special Disney Wedding Dress Collection.

From cuddly Olaf plush toys to fun stationery, Frozen brings its magic into everyday life through a wonderful array of consumer products. Did you know? About 40 dolls found new homes every minute between 2019 and 2022!
Unique experiences, like the limited-time Frozen OH MY CAFÉ for the film’s 10th anniversary, offered fans a celebratory menu of Frozen-themed bites.

With millions of subscribing households, Disney+ provides a powerful platform to expand the world of Frozen. Viewers enjoy fresh, exclusive content, including the platform’s original short animation Once Upon a Snowman.

outro.text: Today, Frozen continues to inspire fans across generations. As the countdown to Frozen 3 begins, the enchanting world of Arendelle is poised to reveal even more frosty adventures and heartwarming moments that will captivate our hearts and spark imagination once again.
